body: Chain-of-thought TTS systems rely on language-model planners to translate persona and context into vocal delivery, but it is unclear where this intent is lost when the requested affect conflicts with lexical sentiment. We introduce a bilingual Japanese--English persona--line conflict benchmark in which each item pairs one line with congruent and conflicting personas and pre-declares the expected acoustic direction. We probe this direction in the planner-generated delivery phrase, the planner-written emotion vector, the QwenEmotion-generated vector, and the rendered waveform. Planner outputs are usually direction-correct, while downstream agreement can be substantially lower. Bypassing QwenEmotion provides only modest gains over the full planner-controlled Base. Supervising QwenEmotion raises the direction rate to 75% in Japanese and 84% in English. A learned text-to-latent interface reaches the highest English rate of 89% and the highest Japanese arousal rate of 88%. These results show that learned repair of the plan-to-synthesis interface can recover counter-textual delivery, although its effect differs across languages and acoustic axes.
summaryZh: 当角色与台词相矛盾时：诊断思想链 TTS 中的计划到综合失败。思想链 TTS 系统依赖于语言模型规划器将角色和上下文翻译成声音传递，但是当所请求的影响与词汇情感冲突时，尚不清楚这种意图在哪里丢失。我们引入了一种双语日语-英语角色-线路冲突基准，其中每个项目将一条线路与一致和冲突的角色配对，并预先声明预期的声学方向。
